sounds.intro: Hungarian is written in the Latin alphabet. It is not related to its neighbours, and it sounds very different. There are no genders and no articles for "a", only "a / az" for "the". The stress is always on the first syllable.
rows: like "d" and "y" together, as in "did you"
like "t" and "y" together, as in "got you"
say "ur" with rounded lips; ő is longer
say "ee" with rounded lips; ű is longer
notes: Hungarian words get endings instead of small words. "Budapest" + "-ben" is "in Budapest": Budapesten.
Vowel harmony: a word uses either back vowels (a, o, u) or front vowels (e, i, ö, ü) in its endings: ház-ban (in the house), kert-ben (in the garden).

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Hungarian often drops the pronoun, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. There is no he / she difference: "ő" means both. "Te" is informal and "ön" is formal.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -k to the noun. After a vowel it is -k; after a consonant it adds a vowel first: könyv, könyvek. After a number, the noun stays singular: két könyv (two book).

grammar.title: To be: lenni
text: In the present, "van" (is) is dropped with adjectives and nouns for he and she. Learn: vagyok, vagy, van, vagyunk, vagytok, vannak.

grammar.title: Van: have
text: Hungarian says "to me there is": nekem van (I have), neked van (you have), neki van (he has). The owned thing takes an ending: nekem van autóm.

grammar.title: Present tense
text: The verb ending shows the person. Dolgozni (to work): dolgozom, dolgozol, dolgozik, dolgozunk, dolgoztok, dolgoznak.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The usual order is who, what, verb, but Hungarian is flexible. The word you stress goes first. "A" or "az" means "the".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "nem" before the verb: megyek (I go), nem megyek (I do not go). For "there is not", use "nincs" or "nincsenek".
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: The word order does not change. Just raise your voice at the end. You can also add the little ending "-e" in written Hungarian.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words usually come just before the verb.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: The owned thing takes an ending: -m (my), -d (your), -ja / -e (his, her), -nk (our), -tok (your, formal), -juk (their): könyvem, könyved, könyve. To like something, use "szeretni".

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: te (informal): friends, family, children. ön (formal): strangers, older people, work. The verb ending changes: vagy / van, beszélsz / beszél.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: add -t- to the stem and the person ending: mentem (I went). Future: "fogok" + the basic verb: fogok menni (I will go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the stem with a vowel (gyere). Formal: a different form (jöjjön). To forbid, put "ne" in front: ne gyere.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Tudni (can): tudok + basic verb. Kell (must): mennem kell. Akarni (want): menni akarok.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Hungarian uses endings, not words in front: -ban / -ben (in), -on / -en / -ön (on), -nál / -nél (at), -ba / -be (into), -tól / -től (from). The vowel follows harmony.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
a macska az asztal alatt van
o MOCH-ko oz OS-tol O-lott von
the shop is next to the bank
a bolt a bank mellett van
o bolt o bonk MEL-lett von
the park is near the station
a park az állomás közelében van
o pork oz AHL-lo-mahsh KUR-zeh-lay-ben von
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -bb for "more": nagy, nagyobb. For "the most" put "leg-" in front: legnagyobb. "Than" is "mint".
